best-broadway-shows.intro:

Lin-Manuel Miranda's Hamilton continues its reign as the highest-rated show on Broadway, with critics still marveling at its revolutionary approach to musical storytelling nearly a decade after its debut. The production's fusion of hip-hop, R&B, and traditional musical theater remains as vital and groundbreaking as ever, earning a remarkable 91 out of 100 from critics.

Among newer productions, Cole Escola's Oh, Mary! has emerged as a critical darling, with reviewers praising its dizzyingly funny take on historical farce. The show's campy absurdity has struck a chord with audiences and critics alike, proving that irreverent comedy still has a powerful place on Broadway. Meanwhile, Maybe Happy Ending offers something entirely different—an intimate robot rom-com that critics describe as refreshingly original and emotionally resonant, demonstrating Broadway's willingness to embrace unconventional narratives.

Julie Taymor's innovative puppetry continues to captivate more than two decades into its run, while the Cursed Child dazzles with stagecraft that critics consistently describe as stunning.

With an average critic score of 86 out of 100 across the top-rated productions, November 2026 represents an excellent time to experience Broadway at its finest. Explore the current lineup to find the show that speaks to your theatrical tastes.
